title: Audit server command-state response matrix
description: Systematically verify server behavior for state-dependent NNTP responses across supported commands: no selected group/current article, nonexistent article selectors, unsupported commands, syntax errors, posting disabled, transfer unavailable, auth/TLS unavailable, and advertised-vs-implemented capabilities. Add or adjust tests where current evidence is missing or indirect.

title: Audit benchmark client/server workloads after RFC strictness
description: Review benchmark fixtures and workloads after RFC strictness changes. Ensure response_parsing, client_roundtrip, client_overheads, server_roundtrip, and server_callgrind measure valid benchmark paths rather than invalid parser fast-fails, and document which fixtures intentionally exercise rejection paths.

title: Run final Nix validation gate for RFC audit
description: Before declaring the compliance audit complete, run and record the final gate under nix develop: cargo fmt --check, cargo test rfc, cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo build --benches, and git diff --check. Treat passing commands as evidence only after confirming the audit matrix coverage is complete.

title: Build RFC compliance audit matrix
description: Create a requirement-by-requirement audit matrix for RFC 3977, RFC 4642, RFC 4643, RFC 4644, and RFC 2980. Map each relevant section/command/response invariant to current tests or implementation evidence, and mark missing or weak coverage explicitly. This is required before claiming full compliance audit completion.
close_reason: Added docs/rfc-compliance-audit.md with RFC-by-RFC coverage matrix and explicit partial/follow-up gaps.

title: Rename green RFC audit tests away from red prefix
description: The rfc*_red_* tests were originally intentional red tests. After making them green, rename or otherwise normalize the test naming so the suite no longer communicates that passing compliance tests are expected to fail. Preserve RFC references and grouping while reducing churn.
